# Results — Study 695 (Inverse Head-and-Shoulders)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **the
inverse head-and-shoulders (three troughs, deepest in the middle) is a reliable bullish bottom;
buy the confirmed neckline break, and the measured-move target (head-to-neckline height,
projected up from the neckline) tells you where price is going.** Offline & deterministic once
cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last
complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Fingerprint `0fed535ace51`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily auto-adjusted (split + dividend) OHLC, SPY + 29 large-cap US names (5,406 rows), 2005-01-03 → 2026-06-30 — the same 30-name **survivors** basket used by sibling pattern studies 415/416 |
| Detector | swing-pivot inverse-H&S: symmetric head/shoulder troughs (`shoulder_tol=0.12`), near-horizontal neckline (`neckline_tol=0.15`), figure span 20–200 bars, confirmed close above the (linearly projected) neckline within 40 bars of the right shoulder |
| Events | **229** confirmed neckline breaks across the 30 names, 2005 → 2026 |
| Statistics | one-sample *t* and **Newey-West (HAC)** *t* on the pooled per-event excess-over-base-rate; a **5,000-draw same-tape random-date placebo** per name (vectorized); a **Wilson interval** on the measured-move hit rate and a **magnitude-matched placebo** (6,000 draws) as its honest control |
| Execution / costs | one documented convention: the neckline break is known at its close (bar *t*); entry is the **next close** (bar *t+1*, one-day lag, zero look-ahead); one round trip = 2 × one-way cost × NAV (5 / 10 bps) |
| Survivorship | **named on the Signal axis.** The basket is 30 names still trading in 2026 — a fixed surviving-names panel cannot include names that delisted after a *failed* breakout, which tilts post-breakout forward returns mildly **up** (i.e. *for* this bullish figure). The result below still fails to clear the bar even with that tailwind. |

## The headline — forward-return excess over the name's own base rate

| horizon | *n* | raw return | excess vs base rate | one-sample *t* | HAC *t* | placebo *p* | net (5 bps) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5d | 229 | +0.326% | **+0.049%** | +0.23 | +0.23 | 0.487 | −0.051% |
| 10d | 229 | +0.954% | **+0.407%** | +1.42 | +1.56 | 0.402 | +0.307% |
| 20d | 228 | +1.058% | **−0.036%** | −0.08 | −0.09 | 0.509 | −0.136% |
| 40d | 227 | +2.315% | **+0.146%** | +0.25 | +0.26 | 0.481 | +0.046% |

No horizon clears the desk's **t ≥ 2** bar — the best is 10d at HAC *t* = 1.56, still short, and
that best-of-four is exactly what a 4-horizon multiple-comparisons scan is expected to produce
under the null. Every placebo *p* sits near 0.4–0.5 — a random entry date on the same tape does
just as well. The **raw** return (+1.1% to +2.3%) looks like a real edge until you subtract the
name's own drift — it is the market's up-drift, not the pattern.

## Detector-strictness robustness sweep (horizon = 20d)

| tolerance | shoulder / neckline | *n* | excess | *t* |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| tight | 0.08 / 0.10 | 153 | −0.300% | −0.52 |
| **base** | **0.12 / 0.15** | **228** | **−0.036%** | **−0.08** |
| loose | 0.18 / 0.20 | 305 | +0.206% | +0.55 |

The (non-)result is not a single-tolerance artefact: tightening or loosening the shape definition
moves the count but never lifts |*t*| anywhere near 2.

## The measured-move target — does "height projected up" forecast anything?

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| signals with a defined target | 229 |
| target hit within 126 trading days | **170/229 = 74.2%** (Wilson 95% [68.2%, 79.5%]) |
| magnitude-matched random-entry placebo (same relative target size, 6,000 draws) | **77.7%** |
| median days-to-hit | 20 |
| mean target distance above entry | +6.4% |

Read alone, "the target hits 74% of the time" sounds like a genuine forecast. It is not: a random
long position aiming for a move of the **same size** (drawn from the observed target-distance
distribution, entered on a random day in the same names) hits it **more** often — 77.7% vs 74.2%.
On a secularly rising 20-year large-cap tape, most 6%-ish up-moves happen anyway, pattern or not.
The measured-move rule doesn't beat the tape's own tendency to drift into striking distance of a
modest target; it rides it, slightly worse than a coin flip of the same reach would.

## The long timer — hold to target-or-timeout (126 days), net of costs

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| trades | 223 |
| gross return / trade | **+2.711%** |
| net return / trade (5 / 10 bps one-way) | **+2.611% / +2.511%** |
| one-sample *t* / HAC *t* (net, 5 bps) | +4.98 / +4.65 |
| average holding period | 55.1 days |
| target-hit share (vs timeout) | 73.5% |
| **excess over a holding-period-MATCHED base rate** | **−0.146%** |
| HAC *t* of the excess | **−0.23** |

The gross/net numbers look great in isolation (*t* ≈ 5!) — but that *t* is testing the return
against **zero**, and a long-only, multi-week hold on a rising large-cap basket is *never* zero.
The only honest race is against a **matched-length buy-and-hold** of the same name (same average
55 days) — and there the excess is **−0.146% at HAC *t* = −0.23**, statistically indistinguishable
from nothing. You would have made the same money buying on a random Tuesday and holding 55 days.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic panel with (a) **pure noise** (no injected shape — the honest null) and (b) a
**planted** inverse-H&S shape with a tunable post-breakout continuation knob (`edge`); no network.

| world | *n* events | Welch/one-sample *t* | note |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| null — pure noise, **20 seeds** (695–714) | ~80–95/seed | mean **+0.028** (sd 1.173), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 2/20 seeds** | detector does not manufacture significance |
| planted edge = **+0.15**, seed 695 | 138 (of 80 planted) | **+8.23** (HAC +9.31), placebo *p* = 0.00276 | detector + inference light up on a real effect |

The detector recovers more breakouts than planted (138 vs 80) because pure-noise segments of the
random walk also occasionally trace a qualifying shape — exactly the false-positive rate a strict
shape rule should have on a martingale, and precisely why the real-tape excess must be judged
against its own base rate, not against zero. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited
in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Forward-return excess over base rate never clears *t* = 2 at any of four
  horizons (best: 10d, HAC *t* = 1.56); every random-date placebo sits at *p* ≈ 0.4–0.5; the
  (non-)result survives a detector-strictness sweep. Survivorship, named, tilts the whole test
  mildly *for* the figure — and it still fails.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The long-timer strategy shows a healthy-looking gross *t* ≈ 5 against
  zero, but the only fair race — against a holding-period-matched base rate — is **−0.146% at HAC
  *t* = −0.23**. Nothing to deploy; costs only make the picture worse.
- **"Measured-move target forecasts the price"? — BUSTED.** The classic target is hit 74.2% of
  the time — *below*, not above, a magnitude-matched random-entry placebo (77.7%). The number
  people quote as the pattern's forecasting power is smaller than the tape's own baseline
  tendency to drift a similar distance.
